note: Human test definitions. Do not record a pass without a person performing the test. Guidepup simulation is not a real screen-reader session.

tests.title: Color alone is not used to convey meaning
tests.purpose: Confirm that a person can tell which kind of message this is without seeing the variant color or icon.
tests.preconditions: Open each alert variant. Hide or ignore color, for example with a grayscale filter or by reading the text only.
steps: Open the informational, success, warning, error, and emergency states.
Read only the heading and body text.
Decide whether the meaning is still clear.
Repeat without the colored border and icon visible.
tests.expected: The heading and text communicate the message type and urgency without relying on color, icon shape, or position alone.
tests.notes: The baseline may pass this check while the experimental theme changes border and background colors. Record which pane you tested.

tests.title: Alert text and boundaries meet contrast requirements
tests.purpose: Measure the rendered text against its background and the alert boundary against the page.
tests.preconditions: Use a contrast analyzer or the browser developer tools on the rendered page. Record the tool and metric.
steps: Measure heading and body text against the alert background in light mode.
Repeat in dark mode if the experimental theme supports it.
Measure the alert boundary and icon against the adjacent background.
Record the measured ratios, not a pass/fail estimate.
tests.expected: Body text reaches at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 under WCAG 2.x. Non-text boundaries reach 3:1 where they carry meaning.
tests.notes: WCAG 2.x ratios and APCA scores are different metrics. State which one was used; do not compare them as equivalent.

tests.title: Alert headings and labels are clear and descriptive
tests.purpose: Check that a heading announces the consequence, not only the severity word.
tests.preconditions: Read the alert in page context.
steps: Read each heading without the body text.
Ask whether the heading describes the problem or outcome.
Check that the heading level fits the surrounding page outline.
tests.expected: Each heading is understandable on its own and does not mislead about the outcome.
tests.notes: Heading quality depends on the implementation's content and cannot be decided by an automated scanner.

tests.title: Each alert variant has a consistent meaning across the site
tests.purpose: Confirm that the same visual and semantic treatment is not reused for a different meaning elsewhere.
tests.preconditions: Review more than one page that uses alerts.
steps: Compare the warning, error, and success treatments across pages.
Check that no other element copies the same icon, color, and heading pattern for a different purpose.
Record any reuse that changes the meaning.
tests.expected: A warning always reads as a warning, and the treatment is not reused for unrelated content.
tests.notes: This test needs the wider implementation, not the single lab fixture.

tests.title: Alert remains readable and functional at 400% zoom
tests.purpose: Check that zooming does not clip the alert or push controls out of the viewport.
tests.preconditions: Use real browser zoom at 400% in a 1280 CSS-pixel viewport, or the equivalent 320 CSS-pixel layout.
steps: Zoom the browser to 400%.
Read the full alert and any links in it.
Check that no content requires two-dimensional scrolling.
Record the browser, operating system, and actual zoom level.
tests.expected: The alert wraps and remains readable without horizontal scrolling, clipped text, or lost controls.
tests.notes: A CSS text-size change is not browser zoom. Do not mark this passed from the lab's text-size control alone.

tests.title: Content survives the WCAG text-spacing overrides
tests.purpose: Check that increased line, paragraph, letter, and word spacing does not clip or overlap the alert.
tests.preconditions: Apply the WCAG 1.4.12 values: line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em.
steps: Open the alert with the spacing preset or a user stylesheet.
Read every line and link.
Check for clipping, overlap, and hidden controls.
Repeat with long content and a narrow viewport.
tests.expected: All text remains visible and usable; no content overlaps or is cut off.
tests.notes: The lab's spacing preset applies these values. Record that this is a CSS override, not a user stylesheet.

tests.title: Screen reader reads the alert in a logical order
tests.purpose: Check that the announced order matches the visual and logical reading order.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader: NVDA, JAWS, or VoiceOver.
steps: Navigate to the alert with the screen reader's reading commands.
Listen to the heading, body, and any link.
Compare the spoken order with the visual order.
tests.expected: The heading is announced before its explanatory text, and links are announced in context.
tests.notes: Guidepup transcripts can help investigate but do not count as this test.

tests.title: Screen reader communicates the alert region or role
tests.requirement: WCAG 1.3.6 Identify Purpose, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
tests.purpose: Check what role, if any, is announced for static and status alerts.
steps: Navigate to a static informational alert.
Record whether a region, status, alert, or no role is announced.
Repeat for an error alert.
Confirm that a decorative wrapper is not announced as a landmark.
tests.expected: The announced role matches the intended behaviour: static content is not falsely announced as an urgent alert, and status changes use an appropriate live role.
tests.notes: Do not add role=alert to content that is already present on page load.

tests.title: Role values are announced for time-sensitive alerts
tests.purpose: Check whether an alert that must interrupt is exposed with role=alert, and whether the interruption is justified.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Trigger the alert yourself.
steps: Trigger the dynamic or urgent alert.
Listen for the announcement and the role.
Decide whether interrupting the user was necessary.
Record the exact spoken output.
tests.expected: The role is announced and the level of interruption matches the urgency. Non-urgent messages do not use role=alert.
tests.notes: Assertive live regions can interrupt. Use them only for urgent changes.

tests.title: Status alerts are announced without moving focus
tests.purpose: Confirm that a status message is announced politely and focus stays where the person left it.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Place focus on the button that triggers the message.
steps: Activate the button that inserts the status alert.
Listen for the announcement.
Check where focus is after the announcement.
Repeat with a second update.
tests.expected: The status is announced without stealing focus, and the updated text is announced when it changes.
tests.notes: This is a human test. The virtual screen reader transcript is supporting evidence only.

tests.title: A newly inserted alert is understandable and not unnecessarily disruptive
tests.purpose: Determine whether a newly displayed alert is announced appropriately.
tests.preconditions: Use a real screen reader. Start with the alert absent.
steps: Open the fixture using a real screen reader.
Navigate to the trigger control.
Trigger the action that causes the alert to appear.
Listen to the announcement.
Determine whether the message is understandable.
Check whether existing speech is unnecessarily interrupted.
Record the result.
tests.expected: The announcement communicates the intended message without unnecessary interruption, and the person can continue the task.
tests.notes: Record the screen reader, browser, operating system, and exact announcement.
